transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-11 14:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Lina Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (TidalGrid CTO), Nora Li (Head of AI), Eric Gold (Infra Lead), Maya Ruiz (Procurement)

Summary: quick renewal touchpoint to confirm capacity bump, formalize private pilot path (on-prem/VPC), and align on security artifacts. Customer wants clearer TCO between hosted vs dedicated vs private onprem and a short pilot to validate latency/cost at 99th p50 and also data residency.

Topics: pricing tiers, dedicated capacity, private on-prem pilot, SOC2/ISO docs, KMS integration, VPC peering, pilot success criteria, timeline

Action items (recap): see action_items above (AE/SE owners).

Transcript:
[00:00] Lina (Redwood AE): All right, hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick audio check?
[00:05] Samir (TidalGrid - CTO): Yep, good here. Can hear you fine.
[00:08] Nora (TidalGrid): Good to go.
[00:10] Lina: Cool. Folks we scheduled this as a checkpoint on the renewal and the private pilot that we talked about — just want to make sure the timelines still work and walk through the requirements. Marcus is here to cover the SE side. Marcus, real quick hello?
[00:20] Marcus (Redwood SE): Hey hey, hi all. I'll cover the pilot runbook and the infra checklist.

[00:30] Samir: High level — we're leaning toward renewing but we need the private on-prem path for data sovereignty in EU and also to push down 99th percentile latency for user facing flows. So main questions: what's the delta in cost and what's the lift for our infra team to run the private pilot?
[00:45] Lina: Great, that's exactly what we want to validate. From a product standpoint there are three levers: hosted API for fastest time to market, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC / on-prem) for data residency and control. Cost profiles change across those.
[01:05] Eric (Infra): Quick clarifying Q: when you say private on-prem, is that fully air-gapped option or a VPC-connect where control plane still talks to Redwood? We have compliance constraints — some teams need no egress at all.
[01:20] Marcus: Good question. We support both flavors. For the pilot most customers start with VPC peering + private control plane — that gives you KMS control, audit logs forwarded to your SIEM, SSO via SAML, RBAC mapped to your IdP. Fully air-gapped on-prem is possible but it's a heavier lift and usually a follow-on.
[01:40] Nora: That matches what we thought. For EU residency we need KMS keys in our region and audit logs retained 1 year. SOC2 is non-negotiable. Can you send the exact SOC2 artifact?
[01:52] Lina: Yes, we'll share SOC2 and ISO artifact links after the call. Marcus will drop the private pilot runbook and the environment checklist too.

[02:10] Maya (Procurement): On the procurement side we need a clear renewal amendment that covers a capacity uplift option — e.g., if we commit to X tokens/month with a three month ramp, what's the pricing tiers, and what are penalties or credits if we burst above? Also need lead time for GPU provisioning for Dedicated.
[02:30] Lina: Absolutely. We'll send the updated pricing spreadsheet with tiered options for hosted vs dedicated vs private. There's also a burst/buffer option for Dedicated that we can include — usually a small buffer you can use once per month.

[02:48] Samir: Competitors — a couple internal folks asked about Bedrock and Anthropic for onprem or private connectivity. Any major gaps?
[02:58] Marcus: Bedrock is strong in some managed infra integrations, Anthropic is more model focused. Our differentiation is the production runtime optimizations, automatic KV/prefix caching, and smart routing so you can route by cost/latency. We'll share some perf slides but the pilot is the best proof. Also you'll see we support continuous batching and quantization profiles which matter for cost.

[03:30] Nora: On perf, we need numbers for p50 and p99 for our shortest prompts — ~64 tokens — and for longer 512 token summarizations. Can you run a few synthetic tests?
[03:42] Marcus: Yep, that'll be in the pilot plan. We'll include baseline tests for 32/64/512 token windows, and a simple KV-cache warm vs cold test. We'll also include memory footprint and GPU type notes — e.g., A100 vs H100 and quantized Llama-style models differences.

[04:05] Eric: On the infra checklist — do you require direct peering or can we use a transit? Our network team prefers to avoid new peering requests if possible.
[04:15] Marcus: You can either peer or use a private link; both supported. For lower p99 it's usually peering, but private link works with slightly higher tail. We'll document the tradeoffs.

[04:30] Samir: Billing question — how granular is the metering? We want token-level breakdowns per route/model so product owners can map cost to features.
[04:40] Lina: We expose token-level cost and latency per model/route in Console. You can down to token buckets per API key and per model. Also cost attribution exports for your BI. We'll attach a sample export.

[04:56] Nora: Security — SSO, SCIM provisioning, full audit logs — are those available for private?
[05:04] Marcus: Yes. In private mode you manage KMS, we integrate with your SAML IdP, SCIM for group sync, and forward logs to your SIEM. Note: for fully air-gapped there are some limitations around auto-updates. We'll call those out.

[05:25] Maya: Procurement — can you give us a template amendment for adding reserved capacity mid-contract? We need the legal language.
[05:33] Lina: We'll include a template amendment and the standard SLA terms. If you want changes to SLA uptime or penalties we can loop legal but typically that's enterprise negotiation.

[05:46] Samir: Great. Next, pilot scope. Marcus, propose a minimal pilot that proves the core risks: latency, cost delta, and data residency.
[05:55] Marcus: Proposed pilot: two-week run in EU region on private control plane with a small reserved capacity (e.g., 4 concurrent GPUs equivalent). Steps: 1) Infra setup (VPC peering + KMS) 2) Model onboarding and quantization profile selected 3) Run benchmark suite (32/64/512 tokens) 4) Collect logs and cost exports 5) Review and decide on uplift. We'll give detailed timeline in the runbook.
[06:22] Nora: Two weeks sounds ok; product wants to see stability under burst. Include a noisy neighbor simulation?
[06:30] Marcus: We can simulate load and also show burst behavior. We'll also enable KV cache warmup to show 30–40% cost drop on typical user flows.

[06:45] Samir: For data residency, once pilot completes we want a certificate that data was stored only in EU and KMS keys stayed in our account.
[06:55] Marcus: We'll provide audit logs and a signed statement for the pilot window. For long-term we'd set up audit-forwarding to your SIEM.

[07:10] Maya: Timeline constraints: we need pilot results before EOY procurement cycle, ideally by mid-July. Is that doable?
[07:18] Lina: Yes, if we kick off late June (we proposed June 21/22) a two-week pilot ends early July and leaves time for contracting. Will include some buffer for infra setup.

[07:28] Eric: One more infra nit: do you support our in-house HSM for KMS or only cloud KMS providers?
[07:36] Marcus: We support bring-your-own KMS including some HSMs via standard KMIP connectors, but we'll need to validate exact model. We'll add it to the checklist.

[07:48] Nora: Pricing — we want the delta between Hosted per-token vs Dedicated reserved seat; specific question: for 3M tokens/month steady and 10M burst, what's the expected monthly? Also, are there discounts if we commit 12 months?
[08:04] Lina: We'll put those numbers in the spreadsheet. Typical pattern: hosted is pay-as-you-go, dedicated gives a lower per-token unit for baseline with committed monthly fee and burst credit pricing; 12-months gets additional discount tiers. We'll provide concrete scenarios.

[08:22] Samir: Any notable limits for private onprem in terms of model catalog? Can we bring custom models?
[08:30] Marcus: You can bring models; the runtime supports common formats. For some bleeding-edge kernels there may be a tuning step. We'll include a model onboarding checklist.

[08:42] Nora: Can you also include a sample A/B testing plan so product can gauge quality regressions vs the current internal model? We need to avoid user-facing regressions.
[08:52] Marcus: Yes — we'll include a simple A/B traffic split test with evaluation hooks and automatic rollback triggers if quality drops below threshold on eval prompts.

[09:05] Samir: Cool. Procurement again — what's the minimum lead time for Dedicated GPUs (if we choose reserved)?"
[09:13] Lina: Generally 4–6 weeks for large dedicated pools depending on region. We'll list exact lead times per region in the doc.

[09:25] Maya: And cancellation terms? We need to know how flexible the committed capacity is if we misestimate usage.
[09:33] Lina: We'll add the amendment template which shows step-down windows and pro-rated credits. For custom terms we'll need legal to sign off.

[09:45] (brief cross talk — audio glitch)
[09:58] Marcus: Quick note — for cost savings we recommend a quantization profile combined with continuous batching and KV caching. In many apps that saved ~30–50%. We'll include recommended config for your workloads after you share sample prompts.

[10:18] Nora: We'll share three prompt families today.
[10:22] Samir: One more: do you have references for enterprise customers who ran private pilots with onprem KMS?
[10:30] Lina: Yes, we'll send 2 case studies and a reference contact.

[10:36] Nora: Also want a short runbook for incident response — if there's an outage we need SLAs for failover to hosted.
[10:44] Marcus: We'll map fallback policies: canary fallbacks to hosted for critical production routes with automatic throttling policies. We'll document expected RTO/RPO.

[11:00] Maya: OK, that's helpful. Procurement will review the amendment once we get it and then loop legal.
[11:06] Lina: Sounds good. For next steps — we'll send pricing, SOC2, pilot runbook, and schedule kickoff. Proposed kickoff dates 2027-06-21 or 2027-06-22.

[11:18] Samir: Either works for infra — prefer 6/21. We'll confirm by EOD tomorrow.
[11:24] Lina: Great. Anything else?
[11:27] Eric: Minor: our infra team will need a Slack channel with an SE for quick triage during setup.
[11:34] Marcus: I'll set that up and be available during the window.

[11:39] Nora: Thanks all.
[11:41] Lina: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs.
[11:45] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcript had occasional speaker mislabels and missed punctuation; some product names transcribed oddly (e.g., "KV cache" as "K V cache") — manual cleaning done for core items but left as transcript-like for authenticity.

Shared artifacts referenced: pricing_spreadsheet_v3.xlsx (link in CRM), private_pilot_runbook_draft.pdf (shared via drive), SOC2_summary_redacted.pdf (link).
